selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing appworker user, then created it and confirmed uid=1000(appworker).

selected_evidence.requirement: Login sessions limited to 8192 open files and 256 processes
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote limits.d config for nofile=8192/nproc=256, confirmed pam_limits is wired into session stacks, and a live login session (su -) showed ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (29011044-...) and uptime start (08:49:48) as the baseline boot identity.
Backgrounded a delayed reboot so the exec call returned 'triggered' immediately, prior to the node going down.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Boot_id was unchanged, then the node became unreachable (connection timed out) confirming the reboot occurred, then reappeared with a new boot_id (d2b40e33-...) and new uptime start (08:50:20).

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required account/data state
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, appworker account, limits.d config file, and effective ulimits (8192 files / 256 processes) were all confirmed intact via a fresh login session.

commands.command: id appworker 2>&1; cat /etc/os-release | head -3; getent passwd appworker
commands.stdout:

commands.command:
printf 'appworker soft nofile 8192
appworker hard nofile 8192
appworker soft nproc 256
appworker hard nproc 256
' | sudo tee /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf
